Hey buddy, spam's still a big problem on the web and it seems like many folks are still falling for bad email habits. A study by the Anti-Phishing Working Group found that 77% of spam emails include links or attachments, which shows lots of people are still opening or clicking on those pesky messages - sometimes ending up with malware or getting phished.

This isn't new, but spammers keep finding new ways to trick us. Proofpoint says blocking suspicious emails at the start can help, but our habits really affect how well those work. Like, people still open emails from unknown senders, click on things without thinking, or open attachments without checking where they came from. It's risky for them and makes it worse for everyone.

Dr. John Doe from Proofpoint says "Email is great for communication but misused can be super dangerous for security." So we gotta stay alert and do safer things like use spam filters, check email sources, and avoid emails from people we don't know. And with so many people now getting emails on phones, it's even easier for spammers to get us. 

Experts say the best way is for users to learn more about how to spot spam and protect ourselves. This means knowing what to look out for, avoiding dodgy links/attachments, and keeping our security software up to date. Businesses should too - have strict rules and teach employees to spot scams.

Jane Smith from APWG adds "Spammers keep coming up with ways to slip through filters, so we need both tech fixes AND for people to know better." In short, while tech gets better, it's still us users who need to watch out and be smart.

Hey there! Just wanted to let you know that with the digital age, cyber threats are getting sneakier and more widespread. There's this new trend where hackers are using unsuspecting PCs for bad stuff. It’s called “hacking through the backdoor” – they get into people’s devices without them knowing or giving permission.

It’s scary because PCs are becoming a bigger target now compared to phones. Hackers usually go after PCs since they’re easier to slip past. They might trick users into downloading fake updates or security patches, which secretly let them look at what you're doing online, steal your info, or even control your PC to launch big cyberattacks.

If your PC gets hacked, it can really mess things up. You could end up having your identity stolen, lose money, or even face blackmail. Your privacy is compromised too, which can be tough for both individuals and businesses. Companies might get bad press, have trouble working normally, or face legal issues if sensitive data leaks out.

To protect ourselves, we should be extra careful. Update our software regularly, use strong passwords, and avoid anything suspicious. We should also use good antivirus software and check our PC often for anything suspicious.

But fighting these hackers isn’t just about us being smart. Tech companies, security firms, and governments need to work together too. They should find and fix bugs before hackers do. We also need better ways to teach everyone about cyber safety and stronger laws to stop bad guys and keep our digital stuff safe.

So, we need to be super aware and take action to make sure our PCs stay safe. The more we all do our part, the better chance we have of keeping our privacy and security.
